name: Intestinal Pseudo-Obstruction

criteria.description: Signs and symptoms of intestinal obstruction (distension, pain, nausea/vomiting, constipation)
Radiographic evidence of dilated bowel (colonic diameter > 6 cm or cecal diameter > 9 cm)
Absence of mechanical obstruction (confirmed by CT or contrast enema)
Identifiable precipitating factor (surgery, illness, medications, electrolyte disturbance)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical features of obstruction with radiographic bowel dilation in the absence of mechanical obstruction.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Acute colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie syndrome) is the most common form. Distinguished from chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction (CIPO), which is a separate entity.

pathognomonic.notes: Often massive; typically develops over 3-7 days

rare.notes: Risk increases when cecal diameter >12 cm or duration >6 days
Consequence of perforation; mortality up to 40%

laboratory: Electrolyte panel: check for hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, hypocalcemia
CBC: leukocytosis may suggest ischemia or perforation
Metabolic panel: assess for hypothyroidism, uremia
imaging: Abdominal X-ray: colonic dilation, often right > left, without transition point
CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast: excludes mechanical obstruction, assesses cecal diameter and wall integrity
Water-soluble contrast enema: diagnostic and potentially therapeutic
genetic: No genetic associations for acute form (Ogilvie syndrome)
other: Colonoscopic decompression if neostigmine fails or is contraindicated
Cecostomy tube placement for refractory cases
Neostigmine test/treatment: rapid decompression suggests cholinergic mechanism

distinguishingFeatures: Mechanical obstruction shows a transition point on CT
Mechanical obstruction has different air-fluid level patterns
CIPO is chronic/recurrent with episodes over months-years
CIPO often has small bowel predominance
Toxic megacolon presents with systemic toxicity, fever, tachycardia
Usually occurs in context of C. difficile infection or IBD

redFlags: Fever and leukocytosis suggesting ischemia or perforation
Free air on imaging indicating perforation
references: Vanek VW, Al-Salti M. Acute pseudo-obstruction of the colon (Ogilvie's syndrome): an analysis of 400 cases. Dis Colon Rectum. 1986;29(3):203-210.
Saunders MD, Kimmey MB. Systematic review: acute colonic pseudo-obstruction. Aliment Pharmacol Ther. 2005;22(10):917-925.
Ross SW, et al. Acute colonic pseudo-obstruction: defining the epidemiology, treatment, and adverse outcomes of Ogilvie's syndrome. Am Surg. 2016;82(2):102-111.
